subject: Agriculture
title: The Steel Plow
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Steel Plow.

hook.text: American prairie soil was so tough and sticky that wooden and iron plows couldn't cut it.

buildup.text: In 1837, John Deere forged a plow from polished steel. The soil slid right off instead of sticking.

discovery.text: Suddenly, millions of acres of prairie became farmable. The American Midwest opened for agriculture.

twist.text: Prairie soil had been built by 10,000 years of grass roots. Plowing it released stored carbon into the air.

climax.text: The steel plow turned the Great Plains into the world's breadbasket—and set the stage for the Dust Bowl.

punchline.text: One tool opened a continent. What it unlocked had consequences.

quiz.question: What problem did John Deere's steel plow solve?
options: Prairie soil stuck to iron plows, but slid off polished steel
It could plow in the rain

details.summary: John Deere's steel plow, invented in 1837, cut through the thick, sticky prairie soils of the American Midwest that had defeated cast-iron plows. This topic covers how this single tool unlocked the breadbasket of the world for agricultural production.
details.whyItMatters: Before the steel plow, the American prairies were considered unplowable. Deere's innovation opened millions of acres of the most fertile soil on Earth, transforming the US into a global agricultural powerhouse.
takeaways: Cast-iron plows could not handle sticky prairie soil—earth clung to the blade
Deere's polished steel blade sliced through prairie soil cleanly without clogging
The steel plow enabled settlement and farming across the entire American Midwest

faq.question: Why was the steel plow necessary for farming the American prairies?
faq.answer: Prairie soil was thick, root-bound, and sticky. Cast-iron plows could not cut through it cleanly—soil stuck to the blade, requiring constant scraping. John Deere's polished steel design shed soil naturally, making prairie farming practical.

faq.question: How did the steel plow change American agriculture?
faq.answer: It opened the vast prairies of the Midwest—some of the world's most fertile land—to large-scale farming. This transformed the US into a global grain producer and encouraged westward migration, creating the American agricultural heartland.
